stem: Identify the process shown in the figure and name it.
solution:
The figure shows NUCLEAR FISSION, i.e. a nuclear chain reaction.
1. A slow-moving neutron strikes a heavy \(\mathrm{{}^{235}U}\) nucleus and is absorbed by it, forming the unstable nucleus \(\mathrm{{}^{236}U}\).
2. This unstable nucleus at once breaks up into two lighter nuclei — \(\mathrm{{}^{141}Ba}\) and \(\mathrm{{}^{92}Kr}\) — and simultaneously releases three fresh neutrons, gamma radiation and a very large amount of energy.
3. Each of the newly released neutrons can strike another \(\mathrm{{}^{235}U}\) nucleus and split it in the same way, so the reaction goes on multiplying by itself. Such a self-sustaining reaction is called a CHAIN REACTION.
4. When this chain reaction is controlled (in a nuclear reactor) the heat released is used to produce steam and thus to generate electricity — this is nuclear energy.
figureNote: Nuclear fission / chain reaction diagram: a neutron striking a U-235 nucleus, forming the unstable U-236 nucleus, which splits into Ba-141 and Kr-92 with a gamma ray and three emitted neutrons; p-00.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: Fill in the blank and rewrite the completed statement: Pranav and Pritee are twins in your class. They belong to ____________ twins' type.
solution:
Pranav and Pritee are twins in your class. They belong to DIZYGOTIC (fraternal / non-identical) twins' type.
Reason: Pranav is a boy and Pritee is a girl, i.e. the two twins are of different sexes. Monozygotic (identical) twins are formed when a SINGLE fertilised egg (zygote) splits into two, so they carry exactly the same genetic material and are always of the same sex. Dizygotic twins are formed when TWO ova are released at the same time and are fertilised by two different sperms, giving two separate zygotes; such twins may be of the same or of different sexes and resemble each other only as much as ordinary brothers and sisters do.

stem: There is an oil layer on the water surface of a river in your area. What will you do?
solution:
The oil spill would be cleaned up by BIOREMEDIATION, i.e. by using hydrocarbonoclastic bacteria.
1. Bacteria such as Pseudomonas (the oil-eating or hydrocarbonoclastic bacteria) can decompose the hydrocarbons of petroleum products; they would be sprayed over the oil layer so that the oil is broken down into harmless substances.
2. The local authorities and the Pollution Control Board would be informed at once, and the source of the leakage would be traced and stopped so that no further oil enters the river.
3. This method is preferred because it is eco-friendly — no harmful chemicals are added to the water, and the aquatic plants and animals are saved from suffocation caused by the oil film cutting off oxygen and sunlight.

stem: Fill in the boxes with the help of the given clue: Continuous consumption of alcohol and tobacco material leads to ____________ . (The word has nine letters; the first letter is 'A' and the eighth letter is 'O'.)
solution:
ADDICTION.
Continuous consumption of alcohol, tobacco or similar substances creates a physical and mental dependence on them, so that the person is unable to stop using them of his own will. This condition is called addiction. (The nine boxes are filled as A, D, D, I, C, T, I, O, N — the given 'A' in the first box and 'O' in the eighth box fit this word.)

stem: Find out the correlation: White revolution : Increase in dairy production :: Green revolution : ____________
solution:
White revolution : Increase in dairy production :: Green revolution : INCREASE IN AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION (increase in crop yield / food-grain production).
Just as the White revolution brought about a large increase in the production of milk and milk products in the country, the Green revolution — through high-yielding hybrid seed varieties, fertilisers, irrigation and improved farming techniques — brought about a large increase in the production of food crops such as wheat and rice.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 1
stem: Somatic and stem cells undergo ____________ type of division.
solution: Mitosis. Mitosis is the equational division that takes place in the SOMATIC (body) cells and in the stem cells: one parent cell gives two daughter cells, each with exactly the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell. It is responsible for growth of the body, repair of worn-out tissues and the replacement of dead cells. Meiosis, on the other hand, is the reduction division and occurs only in the germ (reproductive) cells to form gametes; budding and cloning are not types of nuclear division at all.

stem: Which of the following is a man-made disaster?
solution: Leakage of toxic gases. Disasters are of two kinds — natural and man-made. An earthquake, a flood and the fall of a meteoroid occur due to natural causes and are beyond human control, so they are NATURAL disasters. The leakage of toxic gases happens because of human negligence in the handling, storage or maintenance of chemical plants, so it is a MAN-MADE disaster (e.g. the Bhopal gas tragedy of 1984).

stem: In a food chain, autotrophic plants are present at the ____________ level.
solution: Producer. Green plants are autotrophs — they prepare their own food from carbon dioxide and water by photosynthesis, using solar energy. Since they PRODUCE the food on which every other organism of the ecosystem ultimately depends, they occupy the first trophic level of every food chain and are called producers. Herbivores that eat them are the primary consumers, the carnivores that eat the herbivores are the secondary consumers, and so on.

stem: ____________ is a cold-blooded animal.
solution: Snake. A snake belongs to the class Reptilia. Reptiles are POIKILOTHERMIC (cold-blooded) animals — they cannot maintain a constant body temperature, so their body temperature changes with the temperature of the surroundings. The bat, the rabbit and the elephant all belong to the class Mammalia; mammals are HOMEOTHERMIC (warm-blooded) animals and keep their body temperature constant irrespective of the surrounding temperature.

stem: ____________ is a connecting link between annelida and arthropoda.
solution: Peripatus. A connecting link is an organism that shows the characters of two different groups and is therefore evidence that one group evolved from the other. Peripatus has the segmented body and the thin cuticle of Annelida together with the jointed appendages and tracheal breathing of Arthropoda, so it is the connecting link between these two phyla. (The duck-billed platypus is the connecting link between reptiles and mammals, and the lungfish between fishes and amphibians; the whale is simply an aquatic mammal, not a connecting link.)

stem: Complete the following chart:
solution:
The central box reads 'Evidences of Evolution'. The four surrounding boxes are filled as follows:
1. Morphological evidence — the study of the external form and structure of organisms; a graded series of similar structures among different organisms shows that they arose from a common ancestor.
2. Palaeontological evidence — the study of fossils, i.e. the preserved remains of organisms that lived in the remote past; the deeper the stratum in which a fossil is found, the older it is, and the fossils show a gradual change from simple to complex forms.
3. Similarities in bone structure (anatomical evidence) — the forelimbs of a man, a bat, a whale, a horse and a bird are used for very different functions, yet they are built on the same basic bone plan (humerus, radio-ulna, carpals, metacarpals, phalanges). Such homologous organs indicate a common ancestry.
4. Embryological evidence — the early embryos of fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals look remarkably alike (all show gill slits and a tail), which shows that all these vertebrates are related and have evolved from a common ancestor.
(Connecting links and vestigial organs are also accepted as evidences of evolution.)
figureNote: Blank concept chart: a central rounded box labelled 'Evidences of Evolution' with four arrows pointing to four EMPTY boxes (two above, two below) that the student must fill in; p-01.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 1
stem:
Draw a neat diagram of the structure of chromosome and label the parts:
(a) Centromere
(b) p-arm
solution:
Draw a metaphase chromosome as a stout X-shaped structure formed of two identical sister chromatids joined at a narrow constriction, and label it as follows:
1. Centromere — the narrow constricted point at which the two chromatids are joined; the spindle fibres attach here during cell division. It divides the chromosome into two arms.
2. p-arm — the SHORTER of the two arms of the chromosome, lying above the centromere. (The longer arm below the centromere is the q-arm.)
Also show that the chromosome is made up of a tightly coiled thread of DNA wound round histone proteins (chromatin fibre) which uncoils into a long thin thread when the cell is not dividing.
The diagram must be neat, drawn in pencil, of a good size, with straight label lines that do not cross, and titled 'Structure of a chromosome'.

stem: What are the advantages of hydroelectric power generation?
solution:
Advantages of hydroelectric power generation:
1. No fuel is burnt in a hydroelectric power station, so there is no pollution of the kind caused by the combustion of coal or oil — no smoke, no ash and no oxides of sulphur or carbon are produced.
2. If there is sufficient water stored in the dam, electricity can be generated as and when it is needed, so the supply can be matched to the demand.
3. Although the water of the reservoir is used up for generating power, the reservoir is refilled every rainy season, so the source is renewable and power generation can go on uninterrupted.
4. The running cost is very low, since flowing water is free, and the dam also gives the additional benefits of irrigation, flood control, water supply and fisheries.

stem: State any four benefits of animal classification.
solution:
Any four of the following benefits of animal classification:
1. The study of a few animals from a group gives us an idea about that entire animal group, so the enormous variety of animals can be studied conveniently.
2. Animals can be identified easily and with great accuracy, because each group is defined by definite characters.
3. The study of animals becomes systematic and convenient instead of being scattered and confusing.
4. It gives an idea about the evolution of animals — how simpler forms gave rise to more complex forms.
5. It helps us to understand the various adaptations shown by animals to their surroundings.
6. It helps us to understand the habitat of each animal and its exact role in nature.
7. It helps us to understand the relationship of animals with one another and with other living organisms.

stem: State any four objectives of disaster management.
solution:
Any four of the following objectives of disaster management:
1. To save human life by moving people away from the place of the disaster to a safer place.
2. To supply essential commodities — food, drinking water, clothing, medicines and shelter — to the affected people so that the effect of the disaster is reduced.
3. To restore normal human life in the disaster-affected region as quickly as possible (restoring roads, electricity, water supply and communication).
4. To rehabilitate the affected and displaced victims of the disaster.
5. To take preventive measures so that the intensity and the damage of future disasters are reduced.

stem: Give scientific reason: Microbial enzymes are used instead of a chemical catalyst in a chemical industry.
solution:
Microbial enzymes are preferred to chemical catalysts in the chemical industry because:
1. Microbial enzymes are active at low temperature, low pressure and mild pH, whereas a chemical catalyst usually needs a high temperature and a high pressure. Hence energy is saved and costly corrosion-proof (erosion-proof) equipment is not necessary.
2. Enzymes are highly SPECIFIC — each enzyme catalyses only one particular reaction — so unnecessary by-products are not formed, and the trouble and expense of eliminating and decomposing waste material are avoided.
3. Because the product is obtained almost pure, the expenditure on purification is minimised.
4. Enzymes are biodegradable and eco-friendly, they cause no pollution, and they can be recovered and reused.
Hence microbial enzymes are used instead of chemical catalysts in a chemical industry.

A person who is in need can receive a vital organ from the donor and thereby get a new lease of life — the lives of many people can be saved, blind persons can regain their vision, and the body can also be made available for research in medical studies.

stem: Name any four organs that can be donated.
solution: Any four of the following organs can be donated: kidneys, heart, heart valves, liver, eyes (cornea) and skin. (Lungs, pancreas and bone marrow are also donated.)

stem: What do you mean by central dogma?
solution: The synthesis of the appropriate proteins by DNA through RNA is called the CENTRAL DOGMA of molecular biology. It states the one-way flow of genetic information: \(\mathrm{DNA \rightarrow RNA \rightarrow Protein}\), i.e. DNA first forms a complementary strand of RNA (transcription) and this RNA then directs the joining of amino acids in the proper order to form a specific protein (translation). This concept was put forward by Francis Crick.

stem: What is transcription?
solution: The process by which a molecule of RNA is synthesised complementary to one strand of the DNA molecule is called TRANSCRIPTION. The two strands of DNA separate, and on the template strand the free ribonucleotides are arranged according to the base-pairing rule (adenine of DNA pairs with uracil of RNA, thymine with adenine, cytosine with guanine and guanine with cytosine). The messenger RNA so formed carries the genetic message of the gene out of the nucleus to the ribosome, where the protein is made.

stem: What is meant by triplet codon?
solution: The code for each amino acid on the messenger RNA consists of a sequence of THREE nucleotides (three nitrogenous bases); such a group of three bases is called a TRIPLET CODON. For example, the codon AUG codes for methionine and UUU codes for phenylalanine. Since there are four bases, \(4^3 = 64\) different triplet codons are possible, and it is the order of these codons on the mRNA that decides the order in which the amino acids are joined to form a particular protein.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 1
stem: Complete the following chart and state which process of energy production it represents:
solution:
The chart represents AEROBIC RESPIRATION (aerobic cellular respiration), i.e. the complete oxidation of food in the presence of oxygen.

The blank boxes are filled as follows:
1. The top middle box = Carbohydrates (the third food type, along with Lipids and Proteins).
2. The box below 'Proteins' = Amino acids (proteins are first broken down into amino acids).
3. The box below 'Glycolysis' = Pyruvic acid (glycolysis converts one molecule of glucose into two molecules of pyruvic acid in the cytoplasm).
4. The common box into which fatty acids, pyruvic acid and amino acids all lead = Acetyl-CoA.

The completed pathway is therefore:
Lipids \(\rightarrow\) Fatty acids, Carbohydrates \(\rightarrow\) Glycolysis \(\rightarrow\) Pyruvic acid, Proteins \(\rightarrow\) Amino acids; all three lead to Acetyl-CoA \(\rightarrow\) Krebs cycle \(\rightarrow \mathrm{CO_2 + H_2O}\) + Energy.

Thus carbohydrates, fats and proteins all enter a common pathway through acetyl-CoA, are completely oxidised in the Krebs cycle inside the mitochondria, and release carbon dioxide, water and a large amount of energy (38 ATP per glucose molecule).
figureNote: Flow-chart of energy production with four EMPTY boxes to be filled: row 1 = Lipids, [blank], Proteins; row 2 = Fatty acids, Glycolysis, [blank]; then [blank] under Glycolysis, a common [blank] box, then Krebs Cycle, then CO2 + H2O + Energy; p-03.

stem: Playing games on the mobile while eating is right or wrong? Justify.
solution:
Playing games on the mobile while eating is WRONG.
1. Food deserves respect; eating should be done in a disciplined and attentive way.
2. When the attention is on the mobile game the person eats mechanically and does not chew the food properly, so saliva does not mix with it well and digestion is impaired; this leads to indigestion and acidity.
3. Such distracted eating also leads to over-eating, because the person does not notice when the stomach is full, and this causes obesity.
4. Continuous use of the mobile in this way becomes a habit and finally an addiction, which harms the eyes, the posture and the mental health of the person, and it also spoils the family conversation that a shared meal is meant to encourage.
Hence one should keep the mobile away while eating.
figureNote: Cartoon picture of a boy sitting at a dining table, eating with his right hand while operating a mobile phone with his left hand; p-03.

stem: What do you conclude from the following picture?
solution:
The picture shows four symbols, each crossed out — a lighted cigarette, a syringe (injecting drugs), a person consuming tobacco/gutkha, and a bottle of alcohol. All four are struck out with a red cross or set inside a red 'no entry' circle.
Conclusion: the picture gives the message that one should ALWAYS STAY AWAY FROM ADDICTIONS such as smoking, tobacco, drugs and alcohol. These substances create physical and mental dependence and cause serious diseases (cancer, liver damage, lung disease, AIDS through shared needles), destroy the family's peace and money, and lower the social health of the community. Hence the picture is an appeal for the control and prevention of addiction.
figureNote: Four crossed-out anti-addiction symbols: a lighted cigarette in a red prohibition circle, a syringe injecting an arm with a red cross, a person consuming tobacco with a red cross, and an alcohol bottle in a red prohibition circle; p-03.

stem: Observe the following picture and state what can be the outcome?
solution:
The picture shows a person standing in the middle of a road and taking a selfie on a mobile phone while a car is speeding towards him from behind.
Outcome: a selfie taken in the middle of the road may well result in an ACCIDENT. The person's attention is entirely on the mobile screen, so he neither sees nor hears the approaching vehicle, and the driver has too little time and distance to stop. Such a 'killfie' can cause serious injury or even the death of the person, and it also endangers the driver and the other users of the road.
Hence one should never use a mobile phone or take selfies while standing on a road, crossing a road, driving or travelling.
figureNote: Cartoon picture of a person standing in the middle of a road taking a selfie with a mobile phone while a red car speeds towards him from behind; p-04.

context: Observe the diagram of the power plant and answer the questions.
stem: Which energy is generated from the power plant?
solution: ELECTRICAL ENERGY (electricity) is generated from this power plant. In the diagram the fuel is burnt in the combustion chamber; the hot, high-pressure gases produced there rotate the gas turbine, the turbine shaft rotates the coil of the generator, and the generator converts this mechanical energy into electrical energy. The spent hot gases are let out as the emission of hot gases.
figureNote: Block diagram of a gas-turbine power plant: 'Fuel' → 'Combustion chamber' → 'Emission of hot gases'; a compressor and a 'Gas turbine' on a common shaft driving a 'Generator'; p-04.

context: Observe the diagram of the power plant and answer the questions.
stem: State its source.
solution: The source of the energy is NATURAL GAS — the fuel shown entering the combustion chamber in the diagram is natural gas, which is burnt to produce the hot gases that drive the gas turbine. Natural gas is a fossil fuel consisting mainly of methane, \(\mathrm{CH_4}\).
figureNote: Block diagram of a gas-turbine power plant: 'Fuel' → 'Combustion chamber' → 'Emission of hot gases'; a compressor and a 'Gas turbine' on a common shaft driving a 'Generator'; p-04.

context: Observe the diagram of the power plant and answer the questions.
stem: Which is more eco-friendly — power generation from coal or power generation from natural gas? Why?
solution:
Power generation from NATURAL GAS is more eco-friendly than power generation from coal.
1. Burning natural gas does not produce sulphur dioxide, \(\mathrm{SO_2}\), which is the gas responsible for acid rain and for serious air pollution; coal contains sulphur and always gives \(\mathrm{SO_2}\) on burning.
2. Coal also leaves behind a large quantity of ash and fly-ash and gives out smoke and dust particles, whereas natural gas burns cleanly and leaves almost no residue.
3. The efficiency of power generation from natural gas is high, so less fuel is burnt and less carbon dioxide is released per unit of electricity generated.
Hence natural gas is the more eco-friendly fuel of the two.
figureNote: Block diagram of a gas-turbine power plant: 'Fuel' → 'Combustion chamber' → 'Emission of hot gases'; a compressor and a 'Gas turbine' on a common shaft driving a 'Generator'; p-04.

context: Identify my class/phylum and give one example of it.
stem: I have mammary glands and exoskeleton in the form of hair.
solution:
Class: MAMMALIA (phylum Chordata).
The presence of mammary glands, which secrete milk to feed the young ones, and of an exoskeleton of hair on the skin are the two characteristic features of mammals. They are also warm-blooded, viviparous animals with a four-chambered heart and a muscular diaphragm.
Examples: cat, dog, man (also cow, bat, whale).

context: Identify my class/phylum and give one example of it.
stem: We form the highest number of animals on the planet. We have bilateral symmetry and our exoskeleton is in the form of chitin.
solution:
Phylum: ARTHROPODA.
Arthropoda is the largest phylum of the animal kingdom — it contains the greatest number of animal species on the earth. Its members are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic and segmented, they possess jointed appendages (which is what the name 'arthropoda' means), and their body is covered by an exoskeleton made of chitin, which is shed periodically (moulting).
Examples: prawn, crab (also cockroach, butterfly, scorpion, spider).

context: Identify my class/phylum and give one example of it.
stem: I live in your small intestine, my body is long and thread-like and pseudocoelomate.
solution:
Phylum: ASCHELMINTHES (Nemathelminthes — the round worms).
The members of this phylum are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic and unsegmented; their body is long, cylindrical and thread-like with pointed ends, and they possess a false body cavity, i.e. they are PSEUDOCOELOMATE. Many of them are endoparasites living in the intestine of man and other animals.
Examples: Ascaris (the round worm of the small intestine), filarial worm (also hookworm, pinworm).

context: Observe the following figure and answer the questions.
stem: Identify the process shown in the figure.
solution: The figure shows a MODERN LANDFILL SITE, i.e. the disposal of solid (degradable) waste by modern sanitary landfilling. The labelled parts — garbage, methane gas outlet, soil cover, collection of sewage, processing on sewage and the well to monitor the ground-water level — are all the features of a scientifically designed landfill.
figureNote: Sectional diagram titled 'Modern landfill site', labelled: Garbage, Methane Gas, Soil cover, Processing on sewage, Collection of sewage, well to monitor ground water level; p-05.

context: Observe the following figure and answer the questions.
stem: Explain the process in short.
solution:
Modern landfilling site:
1. The degradable waste that accumulates in urban areas is used for this purpose.
2. Large pits are dug in open spaces far away from the residential area.
3. These pits are lined with plastic sheets as a precaution against the pollution of the soil and the ground water by the leaching of toxic and harmful materials.
4. The waste is compressed and dumped into the pit, and it is covered with layers of soil, saw dust, leafy waste and specific biochemicals.
5. Bioreactors are mixed in at some places; the microbes present in the soil and in the top layers decompose the waste. The methane gas produced during this decomposition is collected through pipes and can be used as a fuel, and the sewage that collects at the bottom is drawn out and processed.
6. A well is provided alongside to monitor the level and the quality of the ground water.
7. The completely filled pit is finally sealed with a slurry of soil. After a few days good-quality compost is formed, and once this compost is removed the landfill site can be used again.
figureNote: Sectional diagram titled 'Modern landfill site', labelled: Garbage, Methane Gas, Soil cover, Processing on sewage, Collection of sewage, well to monitor ground water level; p-05.

stem: What is biotechnology?
solution: Biotechnology is the technology which brings about artificial genetic changes and hybridisation in organisms for human welfare. In other words, it is the use of living organisms, or of their cells and enzymes, together with the techniques of genetic engineering and tissue culture, to produce useful substances and improved varieties of plants and animals for the benefit of mankind.

stem: Explain any two commercial applications of biotechnology.
solution:
Any two of the following commercial applications of biotechnology:
1. CROP BIOTECHNOLOGY — biotechnology is used in agriculture to improve the yield and the variety of crops. Genetically modified (GM) crops, hybrid seeds, pest-resistant varieties such as Bt cotton and herbicide-tolerant plants are some of the areas in which a great deal of research is being carried out. Such crops give a higher yield from the same land.
2. BIOFERTILISERS — micro-organisms such as Rhizobium, Azotobacter and blue-green algae are used in place of chemical fertilisers. They improve the nitrogen-fixing and the phosphate-solubilising ability of the soil, are cheap, and do not pollute the soil and water as chemical fertilisers do.
3. MEDICINE — human insulin, growth hormone, interferon, vaccines and antibiotics are produced commercially on a large scale by genetically engineered bacteria.
4. TISSUE CULTURE — thousands of identical, disease-free saplings of an ornamental or a commercial plant are produced in a short time from a small piece of plant tissue.

stem: Identify the following symbols and state their significance:
solution:
1. The first symbol is a drop of water held in two cupped hands. It gives the message 'SAVE WATER'. Fresh water fit for use is a very small fraction of the water on the earth and it is fast becoming scarce; hence every drop must be used carefully — leaking taps must be repaired, rainwater must be harvested and waste water must be recycled and reused.
2. The second symbol is a bicycle. It suggests the 'USE OF BICYCLES'. A bicycle needs no petrol or diesel, releases no exhaust gases and makes no noise, so it is the best eco-friendly, non-polluting vehicle; using it for short journeys saves fossil fuel, reduces air pollution and also keeps the rider healthy.
figureNote: Two symbols side by side: (1) a blue water drop cradled in two black cupped hands, (2) a black line drawing of a bicycle; p-05.

stem: How can biodiversity be conserved?
solution:
Biodiversity can be conserved in the following ways:
1. By protecting the rare and endangered species of organisms and by running special projects for their conservation (for example Project Tiger, Project Elephant, the crocodile project).
2. By declaring ecologically important regions as 'biosphere reserves' (bioreserves).
3. By establishing national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, zoos and botanical gardens where plants and animals are protected in their natural or in a near-natural habitat.
4. By conserving ALL the plants and animals of a region — not merely the attractive or the useful ones — because every species has a role in the food web.
5. By framing and strictly observing acts and rules such as the Wildlife Protection Act, and by banning poaching and illegal trade in wildlife.
6. By maintaining a record of the traditional knowledge about local plants and animals, and by preserving germplasm in seed banks and gene banks.
7. By creating public awareness about the importance of biodiversity and by controlling pollution and deforestation.

stem: 'Gender of a child is determined by the male partner of a couple.' Draw a diagram explaining the above statement.
solution:
Draw a cross showing the sex chromosomes of the parents and label it as follows:
Father \((44 + XY)\) and Mother \((44 + XX)\) at the top; below the father two kinds of sperms, \((22 + X)\) and \((22 + Y)\), and below the mother only one kind of oocyte, \((22 + X)\); arrows crossing to give the two possible zygotes, \((44 + XX)\) = daughter and \((44 + XY)\) = son.

Explanation from the diagram:
1. The male produces two types of sperms — one carrying an X chromosome and the other carrying a Y chromosome — in equal numbers.
2. The mother has only X-bearing oocytes, so she can contribute nothing but an X chromosome.
3. Thus the sperm which fertilises the oocyte decides the sex of the child. If an X-bearing sperm fertilises the oocyte the zygote is \(44 + XX\) and a DAUGHTER is born; if a Y-bearing sperm fertilises the oocyte the zygote is \(44 + XY\) and a SON is born.
4. Hence the gender of the child is determined by the male partner of the couple, and the chance of a son and of a daughter is 50% each. It is therefore quite wrong to blame the mother for the sex of the child.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: Prepare a slogan for the campaign against female foeticide.
solution:
Any suitable, meaningful slogan against female foeticide is accepted, for example:
1. 'Daughters give a lot of joy; it is not only the boy! Save the girl child.'
2. 'A daughter is a gift, not a burden — let her be born, let her live.'
3. 'Kill the evil practice, not the girl child.'
4. 'Save the girl child today, save the family of tomorrow.'
(Note: determination of the sex of the unborn child and female foeticide are punishable offences under the PCPNDT Act.)

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: In the following figure, explain how new fungal colonies of mucor are formed.
solution:
Mucor is a fungus with a filamentous (thread-like) body called the mycelium, which is made up of hyphae. Some of the hyphae grow upwards as erect stalks called SPORANGIOPHORES, and each of these bears a knob-like SPORANGIUM at its tip, as shown in the figure.
1. Numerous minute spores are produced inside each sporangium by repeated division of the nucleus.
2. When the spores are ripe the wall of the sporangium bursts and the spores are set free into the air, where they are carried away by wind and water.
3. Wherever such a spore falls on a moist and warm substratum (for example stale bread or a rotting fruit) it germinates, gives out hyphae and grows into a new fungal colony of Mucor.
Thus new colonies of Mucor are formed by SPORE FORMATION (sporulation).
figureNote: Diagram of Mucor: branched mycelium with three erect sporangiophores each bearing a knob-like sporangium at the tip, one sporangium burst and releasing spores; labelled 'Sporangium' and 'Sporangiophore'; p-06.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: Identify and state the type of reproduction represented in the above figure.
solution:
The figure represents ASEXUAL reproduction — more precisely, asexual reproduction by SPORE FORMATION (sporulation) in the fungus Mucor.
It is asexual because only a single parent is involved, no gametes are formed and there is no fertilisation; the spores produced inside the sporangium are genetically identical to the parent, and each spore by itself grows into a new individual.
figureNote: Diagram of Mucor: branched mycelium with three erect sporangiophores each bearing a knob-like sporangium at the tip, one sporangium burst and releasing spores; labelled 'Sporangium' and 'Sporangiophore'; p-06.
